hypotheses.claim: Loom is a Go agent orchestration system with terminal UI, configurable tools/backends and persistent conversation state.
hypotheses.prediction: Entry points should initialize configuration, provider/backend and session stores, then route requests through an agent tool-call loop.

findings.statement: The partial Loom source inventory includes Go packages for agent configuration/registry/context/memory/session storage, TUI adapters, MCP/Supabase/Teradata backends, artifacts, collaboration and generated protobuf/gRPC gateway files. This establishes file presence, not implementation behavior.

The filenames suggest a Go agent orchestration architecture: a terminal interface fronts configurable agents with tool/backend integrations, memory/session handling and workflow patterns. Exact initialization and request flow remain unverified because source text could not be read with available investigation tools.
